title: What is one eighth divided by one quarter?
description: One eighth is divided by one quarter by multiplying by four and shortening. The answer is then compared with one eighth. Keeko raises the doubt of multiplying the two fractions.
teaching_notes: One idea: dividing by a fraction between zero and one gives a quotient greater than the dividend, even when the dividend is a fraction. Watch for students who multiply the two fractions and get a number smaller than the dividend.

source: Find 1/8 ÷ (1/4) and compare the quotient with the dividend.
video_script.why: A learner sees that dividing a fraction by a smaller fraction gives a quotient greater than the dividend.
video_script.substitution: the numbers of the book's own second comparison, one eighth and one quarter
video_script.anchor: one eighth and one quarter drawn as parts of the same bar
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies the two fractions instead of dividing, which gives a quotient smaller than the dividend
video_script.payoff_line: One eighth divided by one quarter is one half, which is greater than one eighth

final_answer.spoken: one half, which is greater than one eighth

video_script.fraction_reading: one eighth, one quarter, one half, one thirty second
maths_rules: the divisor 1/4 is between 0 and 1, so the quotient is greater than the dividend
the slip: 1/8 × 1/4 = 1/32, which is less than 1/8
video_script.design: A bar with one eighth shaded, and a bar showing how many quarters fit.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the division 1/8 ÷ 1/4 on the board

marks.pose: the division arrives on the board
marks.ask: a question mark glows beside the division

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the size of a quotient.
<bookmark mark='pose'/>Find one eighth divided by one quarter, and compare the quotient with one eighth.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the quotient, and how does it compare with one eighth?

beats.on_screen: the division stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a whole bar cut into four equal quarters

marks.ask: the bar arrives cut into quarters
marks.four: four quarters are counted in one whole

narration: <bookmark mark='ask'/>Dividing by one quarter asks how many quarters fit into the number.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four quarters fit into every whole, so dividing by one quarter is the same as multiplying by four.

marks.given: the dividend and the divisor are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the dividend is one eighth and the divisor is one quarter.

marks.find: the words To find and the division are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the quotient and compare it with the dividend.

marks.mult: the division sign changes into a times sign and the divisor is changed to four
marks.tb: the tops are multiplied over the bottom

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step one, multiply one eighth by four.
<bookmark mark='tb'/>That is one times four on top, over eight.

marks.share: the four and the eight are linked by a line
marks.left: the one and the two replace them

beats.colours: the shared numbers in the accent colour
beats.moves_through: the 4 and the 8 change into 1 and 2
narration: <bookmark mark='share'/>Step two, four and eight share the factor four, so divide both by four.
<bookmark mark='left'/>The four becomes one, and the eight becomes two.

beats.on_screen: the divisor 1/4 is between 0 and 1, so the quotient is greater than the dividend 1/8

marks.div: the divisor one quarter is placed between zero and one
marks.cmp: an arrow points from the dividend to a greater quotient

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step three, the divisor one quarter is between zero and one.
<bookmark mark='cmp'/>That makes the quotient greater than the dividend.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>One eighth divided by one quarter is one half, which is greater than one eighth.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 1/8 × 1/4 = 1/32; the 1/32 is shown smaller than 1/8 on a bar

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows the two fractions multiplied
marks.slip: one thirty second is shown as a very short bar
marks.fix: the bar for one eighth is multiplied by four

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we multiply the two fractions, so the answer is one thirty second.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>But one thirty second is smaller than one eighth, and dividing by one quarter should give more.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>One eighth must be multiplied by four, the number of quarters in one whole.
